name: email-aliases
title: Email Aliases
description: Generate a plus-addressed or catch-all email alias from the website you are currently on. Choose how many domain levels the alias uses, switch between several accounts, and add date or random suffixes so aliases cannot be guessed.
author: jnbp

commands.name: generate-alias
commands.title: Generate Email Alias
commands.subtitle: Email Aliases
commands.description: Creates an email alias from the active browser tab and copies or pastes it right away.

commands.name: build-alias
commands.title: Build Email Alias
commands.subtitle: Email Aliases
commands.description: Compose an email alias step by step with a live preview, an account picker and per-run overrides.

preferences.name: accounts
preferences.title: Email Accounts
preferences.description: Comma-separated list. Use a full address for plus addressing (me@gmail.com) or @example.com for a catch-all domain. Add an optional display name with a colon: Work: me@company.com

preferences.name: separator
preferences.title: Separator
preferences.description: Character between the user part and the alias. Most providers use a plus sign, some use a hyphen.

preferences.name: domainDepth
preferences.title: Domain Depth
preferences.description: How much of the hostname ends up in the alias. Automatic keeps a meaningful subdomain like nas.example.com but drops single sign-on noise like login.example.com. Levels are counted on top of the public suffix, so amazon.co.uk stays intact.

data.title: Automatic — keeps a subdomain only when it means something

preferences.name: stripWww
preferences.title: Hostname
preferences.label: Ignore a leading www.
preferences.description: Drops www. before the domain depth is applied.

preferences.name: dotReplacement
preferences.title: Replace Dots With
preferences.description: Replaces the dots inside the alias, for example example.com becomes example-com. Leave empty to keep the dots.

preferences.name: suffixMode
preferences.title: Extra Suffix
preferences.description: Appends a date and/or a random token so an alias cannot be guessed from the domain alone.

preferences.name: suffixSeparator
preferences.title: Suffix Separator
preferences.description: Character between the alias and the extra suffix.

preferences.name: dateFormat
preferences.title: Date Format
preferences.description: Supported tokens: yyyy, yy, MM, dd, HH, mm.

preferences.name: randomLength
preferences.title: Random Token Length
preferences.description: Number of characters in the random token (1-32).

preferences.name: catchAllTemplate
preferences.title: Catch-All Template
preferences.description: Used for accounts entered as @example.com. Same tokens as the alias template.

preferences.name: lowercase
preferences.title: Normalisation
preferences.label: Lowercase the alias
preferences.description: Also strips characters that are not allowed in the local part of an address.

preferences.name: maxAliasLength
preferences.title: Maximum Alias Length
preferences.description: Truncates the alias part after this many characters. Leave empty for no limit.

preferences.name: action
preferences.title: After Generating
preferences.description: What happens once the alias is built.

data.title: Copy and paste into the frontmost app

preferences.name: browserSource
preferences.title: Read the Current URL From
preferences.description: AppleScript works without any extra install but is macOS only. The Raycast browser extension also covers Firefox and Zen.

preferences.name: preferredBrowser
preferences.title: Preferred Browser
preferences.description: Always read the URL from this browser instead of whichever app is in front.
